title: Derived unit shift transport on single objects
statement: Let B,C be abelian categories with chosen derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], B having enough injectives, G : B → C additive, X : B and n : ℕ. Set S = single_n X as a bounded-below complex, e : single_n X ≅ Q(S) to the canonical single/quotient identification, H₀ = H^0 on D⁺(C), RG = R⁺G. Let c be the inverse single shift on B, followed by the RG shift comparison and the H₀ shift comparison, as in the parent node. Let d : H^n(single_n(-)) ≅ H^0(single_0(-)) on C be inverse single shift followed by the homology shift comparison. Then H^n(unit_S) followed by H^n(RG(e inverse)) and c at X equals H^n(mapHomotopyCategoryPlusSingleFunctorQhObjIso n X hom), followed by d at G(X) and H^0(rightDerivedPlusSingleUnit G X) [lem-sbc-right-derived-single-unit-homology-comparison]. This equation is between maps out of H^n(Q(G(S))) and contains no cycles projection.

source.place: Functor.commShift_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit, lines 245–281; parent proof step 1, single-object specialization. Also Mathlib SingleFunctors and Functor.ShiftSequence naturality.

proof.text: Use naturality of the right-derived unit along the inverse shift identification single_n X → single_0 X[-n]. Apply Functor.commShift_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit at -n. The single/quotient identifications are canonical and natural, so transporting the target produces the inverse single shift and RG.commShiftIso, the first two factors of c. Compatibility of singleMapHomologicalComplex with shift transports the source to the mapped-single comparison followed by inverse single shift on C.

Apply H^n and naturality of the homology shift isomorphism at (-n,n,0), obtaining the final factors of c and d. After transport, the degree-zero unit with the mapped-single and single/quotient identifications is exactly rightDerivedPlusSingleUnit. Both degree-zero identifications are included in its definition. This proves the displayed equation without the homology projection or any classical augmentation comparison.
